demolition.name: Demolition (site + structure at addition footprint)

quantities_used: site_access=direct truck/machine access via side yard

jbd_reference.note: JBD demolition_site_work 20h vs 15h quantity-based; all JBD demo hours map to this single task. Difference is rate, not missed scope — no revision upward.

sizing.hours_basis: 294 sqft paver field lifted/scraped with mini-excavator on site (direct side-yard access) and loaded to the 12-yd dumpster: ~8h (2 people × ~4h incl. bedding sand). 3'x3' concrete sawcut (~12 LF at 4") + break-out + load: ~2h. Masonry fire pit demo (size not given, assumed small ring/box) + haul: ~4h. Protect condenser/wall fixtures in place, tidy: ~1h. Total ≈ 15h. Excavation and gravel base belong to groundwork, gutter removal to the roof tie-in — excluded. JBD 20h runs ~25% high; keeping the quantity-based figure.
sizing.crew_reason: Paver loading is the bulk of the work and goes fastest with 2 hands feeding while 1 runs the machine/saw; heavy paver and fire-pit debris justifies 3 over 2 for one day.
flags: Fire pit size not stated anywhere; 4h assumes a small masonry ring — a large mortared pit could add 2-4h and a heavy dumpster load (overage is CO per JBD).
Hours land at the bottom of the 1-5 wd guardrail (~0.6 wd → 1 wd) — this is a light demo; the 3-4 day hint over-describes a 9 sqft sawcut and one fire pit.
Excludes excavation (groundwork), gutter removal at the tie-in (roof task), and any dump-run travel time beyond the on-site dumpster.

demolition.include_reason: paver removal, fire-pit concrete cut, tie-in gutter removal

site_foundation.name: Site prep (protection, staging, access)

jbd_reference.note: No JBD line maps to site prep; the 42h concrete_patio line is left whole for the foundation task.

sizing.hours_basis: Exterior-only rear-yard job: protect HVAC condenser and wall fixtures in place (hose bibbs, disconnect, meter, lights), lay out slab/post corners for cut, set 12-yd dumpster, stage side-yard access path for mini-ex and concrete truck (plywood/mats at lawn/gate). ~2 people × 5h ≈ 10h. Occupied home but no interior work, so no heavy interior protection. Paver/fire-pit demo is NOT included — it is a demolition scope, not this component.
sizing.crew_reason: Two people to set protection, mats and layout in a morning; one would drag it, three is idle.
flags: Assumes paver demo/fire-pit removal is carried in a separate demo task; if not, add ~20-24h of demo/load-out somewhere — not here.
Post layout must be locked (7-9 posts settled, carried 8) before site layout marks turned-down footing locations.

site_foundation.include_reason: protect rear doors, condenser, wall fixtures; side-yard access

site_foundation.name: Excavation (footings, slab, access)

jbd_reference.note: No JBD excavation hours mapped to this component; gravel base placement is carried here (machine on site) rather than in the foundation task to avoid double-counting.

sizing.hours_basis: 294 sqft strip cut ~9" (4" slab + ~4.4" gravel) ≈ 8 cy plus 8 turned-down post footing pockets and fireplace thickened area, load-out to dumpster/dump run: operator + laborer ~10h each = 20h with mini-ex and direct side-yard access; spread and plate-compact 4 cy gravel base, fine grade to string: 2 × 3h = 6h. Total ≈ 26h → 2 crew ≈ 2 wd. Rock is a change order, not padded here.
sizing.crew_reason: Operator + laborer is the standard TCR dig crew; a 294 sqft cut has one machine workface.
flags: Excavation depth not stated in any source — 9" assumed from 4" slab + 4 cy gravel over 294 sqft.
Turned-down footing depth/size unspecified (IRC in-house sizing not yet done); fireplace footing thickening depends on kit spec sheet (3-4 wk lead) — footing pockets can't be finalized until then.
Tri-Cities rock risk: hitting rock is a CO per canon, zero hours carried.

foreman_adjustment.reason: 8 cy strip cut with a mini-ex and direct side-yard access is a half day, not 10h each for operator + laborer; 8 footing pockets and 4 cy gravel spread/compact are ~6h combined, not another full day

site_foundation.include_reason: 294 sqft dig plus gravel base for new slab

site_foundation.name: Foundation (form, inspect, pour)

jbd_reference.note: JBD concrete_patio 42h covers the whole slab; my quantity build lands at 40h even after adding the 8 turned-down post footings and ~0.7 cy the JBD did not price — the JBD's slab-only figure was slightly hot, the added footing scope brings it back to par. Entire 42h allocated to this task; site_prep and excavation get none of it.

sizing.hours_basis: Forms: ~36 LF free-standing 2x edge form (two house sides get isolation joint against existing foundation, minimal forming) + 8 turned-down footing pockets + fireplace thickened area + 9 sqft fire-pit infill patch, rebar/mesh, screed pins: 4 × 4h = 16h. Footing/slab inspection hold (no hours). Pour and broom-finish 4.5 cy / 303 sqft direct off the truck: 4 × 5h = 20h. Strip, saw/tool control joints, cure cover: 4h. Total ≈ 40h → 4 crew ≈ 2 wd (form day, inspection, pour day). Gravel base already paid into excavation.
sizing.crew_reason: Pour/finish day on 300 sqft broom slab with turned-down pockets needs four hands; forming day could run lighter but crew is sized to the pour workface.
flags: Inherited: JBD prices 5 posts and zero turned-down footings — 8 footings and ~4.5 cy (vs JBD 4.2) carried here.

Fireplace footing thickening dims come from the firebox kit spec sheet (3-4 wk lead); under 'no demo without materials' the spec must be in hand before forms are set — not reflected in JBD's 5-6 wk duration.
Inspection hold between forming and pour assumed one day; a footing inspection is not explicitly listed in the permit answer (framing + fireplace/chimney only) — confirm with Johnson City.
Slab cure before post/beam framing loads (typically 3-7 days) is a schedule gap, not labor hours.

foreman_adjustment.reason: 16h to set 36 LF of edge form plus pockets and a thickened area is double what a 4-man concrete crew needs (~10h); pour/finish 294 sqft plus strip and cleanup is ~16-18h, not 24h

site_foundation.include_reason: new slab pour with fireplace and 7-9 post footings

framing_shell.name: Framing (floor, walls, roof structure, sheathing)

jbd_reference.note: JBD roof 70h is hot (evidence flag agrees: ~50h for a one-plane shed with a beam replacing the ledger); its 48h screen labor is built on 60 LF vs 36 LF settled, so only ~16h of framing share was taken and I carried 17h from quantities; 98h fireplace structure was priced against the masonry option — only the framed chase (~12h) belongs here. Split of my 75h: ~46h roof, ~17h knee/screen framing, ~12h chase.

sizing.hours_basis: Roof structure: 8 posts on turned-down footings (bases, plumb, brace) ~1h crew-time each ≈ 8h; house-side beam 23.5 LF on posts + open-side built-up double 2x10/2x12 23.5 LF (build, splice over posts, set) ≈ 12h; 19 rafters @ 12.5' with birdsmouths at pattern speed ~0.5h each ≈ 10h plus eave tie-in fiddling (gutter off, seat rafters to existing eave framing) ≈ 4h; blocking ≈ 4h; 10 sheets 7/16 OSB ≈ 4h; layout/setup ≈ 4h → ~46h roof. Screen-wall framing: ~33 LF of 2' knee wall @ ~0.3h/LF ≈ 10h + screen-bay/header framing between posts and 1 screen door RO ≈ 7h → ~17h. Fireplace chase: ~6' wide x ~8' tall framed box at the low eave incl. chase-to-eave blocking ≈ 12h. Total ≈ 75h. Chimney-penetration framing excluded (chimney outside roof edge). Firebox/pipe/veneer/hearth/mantel excluded — separate planned task. Screen spline, trim, vinyl finish, door hang excluded — other components. JBD share (~70 roof + ~16 knee-wall framing + ~15 chase ≈ 100h) runs higher; kept my figure.
sizing.crew_reason: Single-story 294 sqft shed-roof porch in a rear-yard inside corner — 3 is the natural workface for setting beams/rafters; more would stack up on a 23.5' wall.
flags: Post count carried at midpoint 8 (7-9 per answer); JBD prices 5 — post/beam material and turned-down footings are missing from JBD
Roof pitch and beam/post sizing not yet done (in-house IRC tables) — no slope factor applied to sheathing/rafter lengths
Chase framing waits on firebox kit spec (3-4 wk lead) for dimensions; chimney termination at low eave is suspect under 10-3-2 and could change chase height at inspection
Framing inspection gates close-in; hours exclude inspection wait
Knee-wall height 2' per proposal governs over drawing's 3'-4" band

foreman_adjustment.reason: 8 posts at 1h crew-time each, 12h for two 23.5' beams, and 0.5h per rafter are day-one speeds; a 3-man crew mid-rhythm sets posts, beams, 19 rafters, sheathing, knee wall and fascia on a 23.5x12.5 shed roof in ~2 days, not 4

exterior_finishes.name: Roofing (underlayment, shingles, flashing, tie-in blend)

jbd_reference.note: JBD roofing 24h vs my ~16h; the extra reads as padding on a 3.3 sq roof, not missed scope. JBD's $245 chimney roof flashing/storm collar is superseded — only a chase-to-eave counterflash remains.

sizing.hours_basis: 300 sqft plan / 3.3 sq single-plane shed roof, no penetrations (chimney outside roof edge). Synthetic underlayment + drip edge ~48 LF (23.5 eave + 2x12.5 rake) ≈ 2h; shingles 3.3 sq @ ~1.5h/sq small-roof rate ≈ 5h; tie-in blend along 23.5 LF existing eave (strip back existing courses, flash, weave new into old) ≈ 5h; chase-to-eave step/counterflash detail at 6' chimney box ≈ 1.5h; setup/ladders/cleanup ≈ 2.5h → ~16h. JBD 24h runs ~50% higher for the same 3.3 sq — kept my figure. Fascia/soffit/gutters excluded per answer; gutter removal counted in framing/eave tie-in, not here.
sizing.crew_reason: ~300 sqft shed roof at ~8' eave has room for 3 (two on the deck, one feeding/cutting from the ground); more would crowd a 23.5' single plane.
flags: roof_pitch unknown — no slope factor applied; a steeper pitch adds a few percent area but not a day
tie-in weave extent into the existing roof is not stated; carried as strip-and-blend along the full 23.5' eave
chimney termination at low eave is [suspect] for 10-3-2 — if the inspector forces a taller chase, the chase-to-roof flashing detail changes and adds ~2-4h here

exterior_finishes.include_reason: underlayment, matched shingles, eave tie-in flashing

exterior_finishes.name: Siding (WRB, siding, tie-in blend)

jbd_reference.note: JBD gives no split; my ~30% share of a de-inflated 29h ≈ 8-9h agrees with the 10h quantity figure. The raw 48h line must not be read as siding hours.

sizing.hours_basis: Siding scope is only the 2' white vinyl knee-wall finish: ~33 LF knee wall (36 LF less 3' door) × 2' = ~66 sqft exterior face, plus interior face if finished both sides (~66 sqft, assumed). WRB on 66 sqft ≈ 1h; vinyl ~130 sqft at ~250 sqft/day 2-man rate ≈ 8h but small-piece work with J-channel/corner trim at ~8 posts, door jambs, and two brick-wall terminations pushes the effective rate down — call it ~7h siding + ~2h trim/J-channel → ~10h total. No fascia/soffit/gutters (excluded), no gable/rake cladding (shed rake ends are screen/transom, not sided). JBD screened-enclosure 48h is built on 60 LF (overstated ~40% → ~29h real) and covers three components; I split it ~40% knee-wall/screen framing (structural_framing), ~30% vinyl finish + exterior trim (this task, ≈8-9h), ~30% screening/spline/door hang (interior_installs) — consistent with my 10h.
sizing.crew_reason: Single-story 2' knee wall worked from grade — no ladders/lifts; 33 LF only supports two hands.
flags: math lands at ~10h (1 wd @ 2) — BELOW the 2-7 wd guardrail; the range assumes a sided addition, but this scope is only a 2' vinyl knee wall — clamp will overstate it
assumed vinyl finish on both faces of the knee wall (proposal says 'white vinyl finish', drawings show beadboard interior — visualization-only, conflict logged); if exterior-only, ~7h
knee-wall height conflict (2' proposal vs 3'-4" drawing) — proposal governs; drawing height would add ~3-4h

rough_inspections.name: Rough inspections (MEPs then framing, bundled)

jbd_reference.note: JBD carries no permit or inspection hours at all (flagged conflict); sized from the permit answer's two required inspections, with the fireplace/chimney inspection assumed bundled into this rough visit since the chase must be inspected before veneer and the roof/chase framing are one visit for the inspector.

sizing.hours_basis: Zero MEP scope (electrical_device_count=0, no plumbing/HVAC), so the 'MEPs then framing' bundle collapses to a single framing inspection of a ~300 sqft shed roof (19 rafters, two beams, ~8 posts) plus the fireplace chase/Class A pipe pre-cover check that the permit answer requires — inspector walk ~1h on site, plus lead/foreman time to stage the visit, open the tie-in and chase for view, and close out the card ≈ 4h total. No JBD line exists for inspections (jbd carries $0 permits); the 2-inspection count (inspection_count=2) is the basis. Hours land far below the 1-3 wd guardrail; the real driver is inspector scheduling, not labor — plan 2 calendar days for scheduling reality per the hint, but the labor is ~half a day.
sizing.crew_reason: Inspection visit — one inspector; crew is fixed at 1 and the in-house lead only attends.
flags: Hours (~4h) fall well below the 1-3 wd duration guardrail — duration here is inspector scheduling latency, not labor; code clamp to 1 wd is expected and should be read as a calendar hold, not work.
Zero MEP inspections on this job — the task's 'MEPs then framing' ordering note is moot; framing is the only rough trade to inspect.

Fireplace/chimney inspection is assumed bundled into this rough visit (chase framing + Class A pipe visible before veneer); if the AHJ requires a separate fireplace inspection, add a second 1-wd hold before veneer.

Inherited [suspect] flag: chimney termination just above the low eave within 10' of the shed roof plane is the geometry 10-3-2 normally forbids — this inspection is where a rejection would surface; a failed inspection would re-trigger chase framing and a re-inspection not sized here.
Inspection holds gate framing close-in (screen/knee wall) and fireplace veneer — a fail or scheduling slip pushes both downstream tasks.
Kit-driven chase dims must be built before this inspection can pass; firebox/Class A kit (3-4 wk lead) is the upstream constraint.
